content:
elaine: Quick RFC follow-up — streaming retries at the edge. I sketched two approaches: (A) full restart on failure, (B) resumable streams with periodic checkpoints. Looking for tradeoffs and safety concerns.
mike: Short take: resumable streams are great for cost/latency but add protocol complexity and state. Restart is simple but wastes tokens and may break UX for long streams. :thinking_face:
hugo: Agreed. Key questions: how do we define a checkpoint? token-boundary only? do we need model-side deterministic resumes? Also auth/authorization for resuming from edge needs thought.
dana: Example failure mode: client disconnects mid-stream, edge loses connection to runtime; if we restart we may regenerate different tokens (non-deterministic output). For deterministic resume we need runtime checkpointing (KV cache snapshot) or model determinism guarantee.
elaine: Right. My rough proposal: runtime emits lightweight resume checkpoints every N tokens (configurable per model/workload). Edge stores a small Resume-Token that maps to runtime checkpoint metadata (not full KV cache). Resume-Token is opaque to clients.
mike: How would protocol look? Something like: client sets header to indicate it supports resume, server replies with Resume-Token in trailer or a header after a checkpoint?
hugo: Prototype header sketch: ```
--> Request: 
POST /v1/generate 
Headers: 
  Authorization: Bearer ...
  X-Resume-Support: 1
  X-Resume-Policy: tenant-checkpoint-512

--> Response (after first checkpoint): 
  HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  Transfer-Encoding: chunked
  Resume-Token: rsm_abc123
  X-Checkpoint-Seq: 1
  
  <chunked tokens...>
```
dana: We'll need to ensure Resume-Token is short-lived and tied to auth context so tenant A can't resume tenant B's stream. Also limit resume attempts to prevent replay.
svc-bot: deploy-bot: Reminder — earlier experiment with checkpointing used ~256KB per-checkpoint memory for Llama2-7B. Keep that in mind when setting default checkpoint frequency. :information_source:
mike: Runtime implications: storing full KV caches per checkpoint is heavy. Alternative: only store small diffs or deterministic RNG seeds + last token sequence so runtime can replay from last checkpoint. That still requires deterministic generation (fixed temperature/seed). Not always possible for non-deterministic sampling.
hugo: Tradeoff table: 
- Restart: simplest, no extra state, worst UX/cost on long streams.
- Checkpoint+resume (opaque token): good UX, needs storage and auth, requires runtime support for deterministic replay or checkpoint serialize.
- Client-side resume (range reads): push complexity to client, but gateway stays stateless — however client must be able to request partial content ranges which is odd for generative streams.
dana: Also consider idempotency semantics. For instructions that mutate model-side ephemeral state (e.g., interactive tool calls), resume might be unsafe. We should mark endpoints as resume-allowed or not. That can be a per-model/per-route flag.
elaine: Operational constraints: edge should not keep large checkpoints indefinitely. Proposal: edge stores Resume-Token mapping in Redis with TTL (default 5 minutes) and caps size per-tenant. If runtime can't serialize checkpoints we fallback to restart.
mike: Observability: emit spans for resume attempts, metric for "resume_success" vs "resume_fail_reason" (e.g., token_expired, auth_mismatch, mismatch_checkpoint). Add token-level cost attribution so we don't under/overbill resumed sessions.
sre-bot: incident-bot: Note that resuming could complicate tracing and replay detection. Include unique trace id in resume token metadata to ensure we can correlate.
hugo: Security note: avoid putting KV cache in tokens or client-visible data. Tokens must be opaque and signed by the control plane (KMS). Also consider rate-limiting resume attempts per token to mitigate abuse.
dana: UX question: If resume fails, do we automatically restart a fresh stream or surface an error to client? I prefer automatic fallback when request is idempotent; otherwise return 409/conflict.
elaine: Proposed decision (consensus from thread):
1) Implement opt-in resumable streams. Endpoint must advertise X-Resume-Support and model/route must be marked resume-allowed.
2) Runtime will provide periodic lightweight checkpoints (configurable). Checkpoints should be serializable diffs when possible; otherwise fall back to restart.
3) Edge stores Resume-Token -> checkpoint metadata in Redis with TTL and tenant scoping. Tokens are signed opaque strings.
4) Default checkpoint cadence: 512 tokens for Llama2-like workloads; make per-model default and tenant-configurable. Memory cap per-tenant and TTL 5m.
5) If resume fails due to auth/mismatch/expired then: if request is idempotent, gateway will attempt restart automatically once; otherwise return 409.
6) Observability + billing hooks required before rolling out.
mike: I can draft the follow-up RFC with APIs and headers, and a small PoC in eng-runtime. Assigning to me + hugo for PoC, dana for security review, elaine for rollout plan.
elaine: Thanks — sounds good. Can we add a note to the RFC about model determinism limits and that some models will explicitly opt-out of resume?
hugo: Yup. Also include a test harness that fuzzes partial checkpoint corruption to ensure safe failure modes.
svc-bot: reminders: @mike assigned: resumable-stream-poc, due 2025-08-04. @dana assigned: resume-security-review, due 2025-07-28.
elaine: Cool — closing out here. If anyone wants to object to the approach, flag before EOD. :thumbsup:
